title: Maximum Total Importance of Roads
summary: Given the number of cities and a list of bidirectional roads connecting them, assign each city a unique value from 1 to the number of cities to maximize the total importance of all roads, where the importance of a road is the sum of the values of the two cities it connects.
statement: Given the number of cities and a list of bidirectional roads connecting them, assign each city a unique value from 1 to the number of cities to maximize the total importance of all roads, where the importance of a road is the sum of the values of the two cities it connects.
constraints: Assign each city a distinct integer value from one through n.
Each road contributes the values of both endpoints, so a city’s label is counted once per incident road.
Return the maximum possible total road importance.
hints: Rewrite total road importance as the sum of label[city]*degree[city].
By the rearrangement inequality, pair the largest labels with the largest degrees.
Sort degrees ascending and take their dot product with values one through n.
Any inversion pairing a larger label with a smaller degree can be swapped without decreasing the total, yielding the sorted optimum.
editorial: Any inversion pairing a larger label with a smaller degree can be swapped without decreasing the total, yielding the sorted optimum.

tests.explanation: Assigning larger values to higher-degree cities produces total importance forty-three.
With no roads every assignment has total importance zero.
